normative_reference: RFC 8785 (JCS), with Soma strictness. Reference implementation: js/src/canonicalize.mjs in hey-vera/soma.
note: These vectors exist to catch a subtly wrong implementation, not to demonstrate a correct one. Every accept case is chosen because a plausible implementation gets it wrong; every reject case is chosen because a permissive implementation silently repairs it.

accept.name: key order is UTF-16 code unit, not locale or insertion
accept.catches: locale-aware sorting, which places 'ä' next to 'a' and lowercases before uppercase

accept.name: nested objects sort independently at each level
arrays preserve order and are not sorted
accept.catches: over-eager canonicalization that sorts array elements

accept.name: integer-valued floats lose the fractional part
accept.catches: implementations that preserve a trailing .0, common in Rust and Python

accept.name: small magnitude switches to exponential at 1e-7
accept.catches: no '+' on a negative exponent, and no leading zero padding

accept.name: shortest round-trip representation, not full precision
maximum safe integer is accepted exactly
accept.catches: off-by-one in the safe-integer boundary check

accept.name: solidus is not escaped
accept.catches: implementations that escape / as \/, which is legal JSON but not canonical

accept.name: control characters use short forms where they exist
control characters without short forms use lowercase hex \u
non-ASCII is emitted literally, not escaped
accept.catches: ASCII-safe output that escapes everything above 0x7f

accept.name: astral plane characters survive as surrogate pairs
accept.catches: implementations that mishandle characters outside the BMP

accept.name: empty containers
accept.catches: special-casing that emits null or omits the member

accept.name: null is a value, not an absence
accept.catches: implementations that drop null members the way undefined ones are dropped

reject.name: lone high surrogate
reject.catches: silently substituting U+FFFD, which changes the signed bytes without telling anyone

reject.name: lone low surrogate
reject.catches: the same substitution on the other half of the pair

reject.name: negative zero
reject.description: -0 and 0 serialize identically but are distinguishable values
reject.catches: normalizing -0 to 0, which rewrites data during canonicalization

reject.name: integer beyond the safe range
reject.description: 9007199254740993 cannot be represented exactly as a double
reject.reason: unsafe integer; encode exact quantities as decimal strings
reject.catches: accepting a value that has already lost precision before canonicalization ran

reject.name: large magnitude is unreachable, not exponential
reject.description: 1e21. JCS would render this 1e+21, but every double at or above 2^53 is integer-valued, so the safe-integer rule rejects it first.
reject.reason: unsafe integer; encode exact quantities as decimal strings
reject.catches: implementations that port JCS number formatting faithfully and then accept values this profile forbids

reject.name: large magnitude below the JCS exponential threshold is also unreachable
reject.description: 1e20. Positional under JCS, still beyond the safe-integer range here.
reject.reason: unsafe integer; encode exact quantities as decimal strings
reject.catches: the assumption that the exponential threshold is where the profile's boundary lies

reject.name: non-finite: Infinity
reject.catches: emitting Infinity or null, neither of which is valid JSON

reject.name: undefined object member
reject.catches: silently dropping the member, matching JSON.stringify rather than rejecting
